note: Stars racing round its centre point to a black hole of at least 8,200 Suns: one of the few medium-sized black holes known, between the Sun-sized ones and the giants at galaxies' centres.
In 1974 the Arecibo radio telescope beamed a picture message towards it: numbers, DNA, a human figure and the Solar System. At the cluster's distance it will take about 24,000 years to arrive.
Not one of ours: it sits at the heart of the Sagittarius dwarf galaxy, a small galaxy found in 1994 behind the Galactic Centre and now being torn apart by the Milky Way.
note_ref: The Staff at the National Astronomy and Ionosphere Center 1975, Icarus 26, 462

open_clusters.about: An open cluster: tens to thousands of stars born together from one cloud, loosely held by their own gravity. They live in the disc and slowly drift apart, so most are young (the ages here are from their stars' colours and brightnesses); the youngest still sit in the spiral arms where they formed.

about: Two lobes of gas and dust thrown off by the star Eta Carinae in its Great Eruption of 1838-1845, still flying apart at about 600-700 km/s. models.unknown: From Earth's side it is Hubble's picture; from elsewhere, an impression. How each spot's light is spread in depth follows MUSE's measurement there (about 1 arcsecond sharp, Hubble 20 times sharper), but the clumps it's split into are drawn in, not measured, and the cloud is kept within about 1.2 times its reach on the sky. Behind the Homunculus, where the picture can't see, its gas is filled in from round it. Depths assume all of it left the star in 1836 and has coasted since; knots from older eruptions (around 1250 and 1550, Kiminki et al. 2016) are really farther out in depth than drawn. Gas moving slower than about 150-200 km/s towards or away from us is lost under the Carina Nebula's own glow: there, each spot's spectrum is bridged from the speeds either side (a guess, not a measurement). Spots MUSE can't measure (field stars, the star's glare and diffraction spike, right round the Homunculus) take the depths of the gas beside them. The Homunculus's outline is left to its model
